name: #57: Activating Ambassadors
description:
As I started diving head-first today into Always’ broader business intelligence (analytics, reporting), I’ve realized there’s a foundational piece of architecture that needs to be established first: formally integrating Ambassadors into the system.

Up until now, the correct focus has been on building out our Affiliate infrastructure. That’s now in a great place. Affiliates can choose whether or not they receive commissions; we can set custom percentages on the admin side... now we’re ready for the other tier in our growth model: Ambassadors.

At Always, Ambassadors are distinct from Affiliates. They are active in the field, cold-calling, running and hosting events, introducing new Members, and recruiting Affiliates. Because of this, their compensation structure is layered:
  • 30% commission on in-person sales at events**
  • 5% residual override on new Members that come in through their Affiliates.
Just like with Affiliates, this % can be modified by Admin.
I believe we already have the Ambassador user role created, but no accounts have been set up yet. Our next step is to:
  • Activate this role in practice (creating test Ambassador accounts for internal use)
  • Define how Ambassadors are attached to Members and Affiliates.
(And we do have two Ambassadors to activate once we're set up... currently, they're set up as Affiliates.)

Once this structure is in place, it will unlock the reporting and analytics we ultimately want (revenue by event, by Ambassador, by Affiliate, and by channel), which is core to how Always will scale this year.

**Although the website only tracks online sales, I'm curious (once we have a BI Dashboard set up) if we can have a way to enter sales after each event manually.  I do not believe Clover has an API that sends sales data out, but this data would be easy to enter, and a very important business metric.

Anyway, I’ll follow this email with my thoughts on Always Business Intelligence (Analytics and Reporting), but I wanted to start by clearly framing why this step comes first.

name: #75: Team Roles and Permissions
description:
I'm curious whether Medusa’s current default role handling is purely cosmetic in our implementation (which I believe Jun told me it was), or whether any real permission logic is already in place.

Because I’d like to move forward with a new development ticket for our admin system.

We need to implement a proper internal roles and permissions structure for the Always admin/backend environment.  Ticket #76 sparked this for me, because I want some genuine Member access control, but ONLY ME.  I'd like some lesser options for access to be available for Josh, Trenton and Danniel, but right now the current role setup doesn't provide for any differentiation here.

Once a team user is assigned a role, I don't have the ability to change that person’s role from the admin side. I can only edit their first name, last name, and email address. Any role change on Always Medusa users or any member access issues (i.e., Ticket 74) currently requires involvement from our dev team, which is not sustainable (especially with the time change).  I want Always to be able to provide very timely and top tier customer support.

We would like to formalize a simple internal staff roles to the following four roles only:
• Super Admin
• Ops Admin
• Support
• Developer

The goal is to create a real permissions system behind these roles, not just labels.

Here is the intended structure at a high level:

Super Admin (Only Me)
This role should have full access and full authority across the system. This includes the ability to assign and change staff roles, manage all member access tools, and access all sensitive administrative controls. This role will only be for me for now and will be reserved for future ownership-level control.

Ops Admin (Josh)
This role should have strong operational access for day-to-day management, but should not have full system authority. This may include customer and membership management, order-related actions, and other operational tools, while excluding the highest-risk permissions such as assigning Super Admin or accessing the most sensitive security controls.

Support (Danniel & Trenton)
This role should focus solely on customer/member assistance and product creation, discounts, channels, etc... It should have limited access to tools needed to help users regain access or resolve account issues, but should not be able to modify staff roles, access advanced configuration, or use high-risk administrative functions.

Developer (You guys!) - All the things!

What we need built:
1. A real internal permissions structure tied to these roles.
2. The ability for a Super Admin to assign roles when inviting a user.
3. The ability for a Super Admin to change an existing team user’s role later from within the admin interface.
4. Clear role-based restrictions on which features and actions are visible or usable by each role.
5. A clean and sustainable structure that can support future administrative tools, including member access recovery tools.

My main concern here is that we need proper operational control on our side without having to submit development tickets every time a team user’s permissions need to be adjusted.

Please let me know your recommendation for the best way to implement it within our current Medusa/Supabase setup.

Thank you!

When someone places their trust in you, they are trusting more than your expertise. They are trusting your discernment. name: #20945 Always Connected — System Design
description:
Hi Nina & Team,
Here is everything we discussed on the call today, along with a quick Loom recording explaining it a bit.  Best to watch the video AFTER reading the system design below.
https://www.loom.com/share/5cdaac91d1c149fabd4d07a79a941075

Also, I would love to set up a meeting with Jun and whomever else to go over this after your review to hear your thoughts and ideas.  Open to all, as you guys usually think of things I haven't.  HA HA

Language and Role Architecture

System layerMember-facing nameInternal meaning
Umbrella ProgramAlways Connected™Relationship-based partner framework
Ambassador-level organizationConnected OrganizationOrganization directly connected to Always; can sponsor and manage Connected Partners
Affiliate-level organizationConnected PartnersIndividual or company enrolled through a Connected Organization


Member v2Partner MemberEnrolled through a Connected Partner; receives Partner Benefits for 1 year before auto-converting to Member v1

Member v3Scholarship MemberEnrolled through a Connected Partner and sponsored through Connected Organization; benefits for 1 year before auto-converting to Member v1


Existing Account Tiers

These remain distinct from the Always Connected membership states:

  1. Customer — public access to eligible non-member products.

  2. Member — standard member (v1) account with full eligible member access; invited by an affiliate or another member.

  3. Affiliate — existing Affiliate (v1) role, directly connected to Always or invited by an Ambassador.

  4. Ambassador — existing Ambassador (v1) role, directly connected to Always; may sponsor events, invite/onboard affiliates, and join members directly.

Always Connected™ adds relationship and benefit records to applicable Member accounts. It should not replace the existing account-role model.

New Account Tiers Needed

  1. Connected Ambassador
    a. Duplicate of regular Ambassador role with modifications of permissions and interface
    b. Removal of My Event Sales section.
    c. Has two links available to share:
         - (1) Connected Partner (Affiliate-level) Membership,
         - (2) a Member (v1)
    c. Can approve both role/types accounts (above) in their backoffice dashboard.
    d. Dashboard shows both types once they "joined". (avoid using the word "recruited")

  2. Connected Partner
    a. Duplicate of regular Affiliate role with modifications of permissions and interface
    b. Removal of Commission Preferences
    c. Has two links available to share:
         - (1) Partner Membership (v2) 
         - (2) Scholarship Membership (v3) 
    d. Can approve Partner Member accounts only.
    e. An Always Admin will need to approve Scholarship Member accounts, but they should show as pending on this user's dashboard.  (Perhaps member type could be added to column?  or perhaps best kept in separate table?)
    f. Connected Partners receive 20% OFF their own purchases indefinitely (just like the current Affiliates do).

  3. Partner Member (v2)
    a. Duplicate of regular Member role with modifications of permissions and interface
    b. Can invite others to join as regular Members (v1) - Currently "Member Invites" tab for regular members.
    c. Partner Benefits Banner at top of Account dashboard
    d. Partner Benefits Banner on all product pages.
    e. 20% OFF for one year, then account auto-converts to regular membership (v1)
    f. Any subscriptions activated during the benefits period (1yr) will maintain 20% OFF price lock.
    g. All notification emails to this member (Partner Member) and to their affiliate-level "Connected Partner" should be unique but identical to the current emails being sent. (I.e. after account request submission, when the account is approved)
    h. 30-day email notification to this member (CC: Connected Partner) when Partner Benefits are about to expire and membership transitions to regular v1
    i. Start date of Partner Benefits is the same as the approval date of the account.  Expiration auto-sets to 1 year from the start.  Always Admin can adjust both these dates in the Admin Dashboard while this v2 Membership is active.  If it has already converted to a regular v1 Membership, account will have to be manually converted to a Partner Member again, and start date and end date will auto-apply once again to 1yr benefits.

  4. Scholarship Member (v3)
    a. Duplicate of regular Member role with modifications of permissions and interface
    b. Can invite others to join as regular Members (v1) - Currently "Member Invites" tab for regular members.
    c. Scholarship Benefits Banner at top of Account dashboard
    d. Scholarship Benefits Banner on all product pages.
    e. 60% OFF for one year, then account auto-converts to regular membership (v1)
    f. No subscriptions available for this member type.
    g. All notification emails to this member (Scholarship Member) and to their affiliate-level "Connected Partner" should be unique but identical to the current emails being sent. (I.e., after account request submission, when the account is approved)
    h. 30-day email notification to this member (CC: Connected Partner) when Scholarship Benefits are about to expire and membership transitions to regular v1
    i. Start date of Scholarship Benefits is the same as the approval date of the account.  Expiration auto-sets to 1 year from the start.  Always Admin can adjust both these dates in the Admin Dashboard while this v3 Membership is active.  If it has already converted to a regular v1 Membership, the account will have to be manually converted to a Scholarship Member again, and the start date and end date will auto-apply once again to 1yr benefits.

Organization Relationship Model

The intended hierarchy is:

Always Connected → Connected Organization → Connected Partner → Partner Member / Scholarship Member

Example:

  • Thank You Life = Connected Organization / ambassador-level organization.

  • Evolve Mind Wellness = Connected Partner.

  • A person introduced through Evolve Mind Wellness is welcomed as being connected to Evolve Mind Wellness.

  • Thank You Life is named as the organizational relationship making the benefits possible.

The member’s primary visible relationship is with the Connected Partner, not the Connected Organization.

Membership States and Benefits

Partner Member

A Partner Member is enrolled through a Connected Partner.

Benefits during the Benefit Period:

  • Preferred Pricing

  • Subscription Price Lock for qualifying subscriptions started during the Benefit Period

When their Benefit Period ends, they transition automatically to Regular Member status. Their account and history remain intact. A qualifying subscription price lock continues after the transition.

Scholarship Member

A Scholarship Member is enrolled through a Connected Partner and receives sponsorship through an approved Connected Organization.

Benefits during the Benefit Period:

  • Scholarship pricing during the one-year Scholarship Membership

  • Continued access to the Always member community and educational resources

When their Benefit Period ends, they transition automatically to Regular Member status. Their account and history remain intact. Scholarship pricing ends, and no Subscription Price Lock carries forward.

A future scholarship requires a new approved scholarship enrollment and creates a new Benefit Period.

Benefit Period Lifecycle

Core flow:

Enrollment approved and member account created → Benefit Period begins → benefits active for one year → automatic transition to Regular Member

Requirements:

  • Start date: the date the enrollment is approved and the account is created.

  • End date: one calendar year after the start date.

  • Benefits remain active through the displayed end date.

  • Member-facing display format: “Benefits active through July 29, 2027.”

  • Store an exact end timestamp internally, while presenting the inclusive calendar date to the member.

  • Benefits do not renew automatically.

  • Early termination or revocation should be supported administratively but used rarely, documented, and handled with care.  Probably as simple as changing them to a regular Member (v1) and then we'll personally email them.  This will rarely, if ever, happen.

Relationship Rules

  • A member may have only one active Always Connected membership relationship.

  • Multiple invitations or overlapping Connected Partner relationships are not permitted.

  • Once enrolled through a Connected Partner, that Connected Partner remains the member’s relationship for the life of the account.

  • The system should preserve this relationship context after transition to Regular Member for historical/account-reference purposes.

Member Dashboard Banner

A persistent Always Connected card should appear in the account area.

Placement

  • Desktop: in the main content column, below the “Hello [Name]” / signed-in row and above the Profile and Addresses summary.

  • Mobile: below the site header and above the account-section dropdown selector so the relationship card is always visible before navigating dashboard sections.

Visual Direction

  • Compact, pale warm-cream card

  • Thin muted-teal border

  • Rounded corners

  • Connected/linked-circle icon at left

  • Orange/gold circular check icons for benefits

  • Preserve the existing Always dashboard design system


Partner Member Account Dashboard Banner Copy

WELCOME FROM [CONNECTED PARTNER NAME]

You’re receiving Partner Benefits through our relationship with [CONNECTED ORGANIZATION NAME] and Always.

Benefits active through [DATE]

  • Preferred Pricing

  • Subscription Price Lock

Example:

WELCOME FROM EVOLVE MIND WELLNESS

You’re receiving Partner Benefits through our relationship with Thank You Life and Always.

Scholarship Member Account Dashboard Banner Copy

WELCOME FROM [CONNECTED PARTNER NAME]

Your Scholarship Membership has been made possible through our relationship with [CONNECTED ORGANIZATION NAME] and Always.

Benefits active through [DATE]

  • Scholarship pricing during your one-year Scholarship Membership

  • Continued access to the Always member community and educational resources


Communications

Required lifecycle communications:

  • Welcome message when account request submitted

  • Welcome message when approved enrollment

  • Relationship-centered message approximately 30 days before benefits end (CC: Connected Partner)

  • Transition confirmation when the account becomes a regular Member.


 Email Copy for Always Connected memberships

Pilot Context

Thank You Life is the initial Connected Organization and pilot partner. Evolve Mind Wellness is the working example of a Connected Partner in member-facing mockups.

The system is intended to be designed to support additional Connected Organizations and Connected Partners later.  We already have an organization that serves veterans and first-responder networks interested.  We will run the pilot with Thank You Life and their partners for AT LEAST 3-4 months to workout any bugs before taking on other organizations.

name: GSC Data
description:
Hope you are doing well! We have been digging into our Google Search Console data across all six of our practice websites and found one issue that keeps showing up that I wanted to flag.


For most of our sites, Google is seeing two separate versions of the homepage and treating them as different pages. For example on Grand Rapids, it is seeing both:
  • http://www.grandrapidsdentalteam.com/
  • https://grandrapidsdentalteam.com/


Because Google thinks these are two different pages, the ranking strength is being split between them instead of all going to one URL. Consolidating these would help our search rankings.


The same thing is happening on these four sites:
  • Grand Rapids Dental Team
  • Grandville Dental Team
  • Livonia Dental Team
  • Toledo Dental Team


It would see the fix is making sure all traffic redirects consistently to a single version of the homepage URL. Our preference would be https, non-www for all sites (e.g. https://grandrapidsdentalteam.com/) but happy to defer to whatever you recommend as the cleanest solution.

Waterford and Willoughby look clean on this front so no changes needed there.

One other small item…on the Waterford site, a Sanity CDN image URL is showing up as an indexed page in Google Search Console. The URL looks something like:

https://www.waterforddentalteam.com/_next/image?url=https://cdn.sanity.io/images/...


Not a big deal but wanted to mention it in case there is an easy way to prevent those from being indexed.

That is it! Really appreciate everything you do for us. Let me know if you have any questions.
